tested:
ROOT CAUSE (2026-07-18, device audit for image "xrv9k-fullk9"): get_profile()
only matches when the normalized image name CONTAINS the normalized key, and
the real catalog image is imported as "xrv9k-fullk9" (folder name, no "cisco-"
prefix) - it never contained "cisco-xrv9k", so it silently fell through to
GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE (512 MB RAM / 1 vCPU / 120s boot_timeout / machine=pc)
instead of this profile's 16 GB / 2 vCPU / 900s / machine=q35. A real XRv9k
image cannot even start IOS XR's control plane with 512 MB RAM, so every boot
guaranteed-failed. "csr1000v"/"asav" already carry this same bare-key duplicate
alongside their "cisco-*" key (see below) for exactly this reason - do the same
here so any "xrv9k*"-named image (with or without a vendor prefix) matches.

reasons.config_dialect:
IOS-XR, not IOS: its config save is a two-stage commit, so the CLI dialect
cannot be inferred from vendor="cisco" (which means IOS). Live-proved
2026-08-30 on a real booted xrv - see VENDOR_CLI["iosxr"] in node_config.py.
reasons.emulator:
machine/nic fix: see "cisco-xrv9k" above for the root cause and evidence -
this bare "xrv9k" key is the duplicate that real image lookups actually hit.
